summary.plain: COHERENT reports the first detection of neutrinos scattering coherently off natural germanium, using an array of eight high-purity germanium detectors at Oak Ridge. The collaboration calls the result evidence: it rejects the no-scattering hypothesis at 3.9σ, and the signal rate agrees with the Standard Model within 2σ.
summary.technical: First detection of CEvNS on natural germanium using the Ge-Mini array (eight 2.2 kg ICPC high-purity germanium detectors, 1.5 keVee threshold) operated at the SNS June-August 2023: an on-beam excess of 20.6(+7.1/−6.3) counts over 10.22 GWh*kg exposure, rejecting the no-CEvNS hypothesis at 3.9σ, in agreement with the Standard Model prediction within 2σ.

title: Evidence of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with COHERENT's Germanium Array
why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says CEvNS had been measured on only two nuclear targets to date; this is a 3.9σ rejection of the no-CEvNS hypothesis on natural germanium, a signal rate within 2σ of the Standard Model prediction, and the collaboration words it as evidence rather than an observation.
